answer: Persistent work ledger pricing. Each identity's reputation is a basalt-like anchor: a slow-decaying score earned only through verified completed tasks, so a fresh clone starts at zero and must redo equivalent labor before bidding. Enforce a spiral rule where every bid requires posting a deposit equal to the median cost of the last ten accepted jobs, refunded only on delivery. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times that deposit plus N times the labor to rebuild an atlas of trust, making honest single-identity operation strictly cheaper.
